answer: Persistent compute-time ledger. Each identity must accumulate a minimum of verifiable CPU-hours on public challenge workloads before it can transact, recorded in a shared onyx-sealed log. Idle or duplicate agents cannot shortcut this because cycles are metered per signed session. An attacker must sustain real hardware and electricity across every sybil, paying roughly one machine-hour per identity per epoch. New identities sit on a waitlist knoll until their ledger clears, and any lotus-style burst of registrations triggers a slower audit queue.
